note_en: 把 lets Chinese put the object before the verb and then say what happens to it: 把一个小摊子做成了闻名全国的大饭庄 "turned a tiny stall into a nationally famous restaurant." The result phrase 做成 ("make into") follows the verb, much like English "turn X into Y," and 凭着 ("relying on") at the start of the clause names the means, like English "with" or "thanks to."
